title: Watermelon, Feta, and Mint Salad Recipe
description: From SeriousEats: Sweet watermelon, salty feta, and mint are a classic pairing. Adding a good dose of chopped lemon zest enhances the aromatic flavors in the watermelon. Crumbling the feta over the top instead of tossing it together with the rest of the salad provides a more interesting finished texture and flavor. Like a classic Caprese — which juxtaposes a sweet, watery fruit with a single herb and a creamy cheese, this Watermelon Salad is much more forgiving when it comes to riffing and improvising (like including avocado or cucumbers or red onions).
ingredients: 3 pounds seedless watermelon (about 1 small or 1/4 large), rind removed, cut into 1-inch chunks (about 2 pounds/1kg chunks after rind is discarded)
1 tablespoon (15ml) juice from 1 lemon, plus 4 (2-inch) strips zest, removed with a sharp vegetable peeler, or just grate a lemon for the zest portion
1/4 cup (10g) roughly chopped fresh mint leaves
3 tablespoons (45ml) extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
Up to 4 ounces (1 quart) arugula leaves (optional; see notes)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
directions: Place watermelon chunks in a large bowl.
Finely chop lemon strips, or use the zest. Add lemon juice and half of zest to bowl with watermelon.
Add mint, oil, and arugula (if using) and toss until watermelon is evenly dressed.
Season lightly to taste with salt and pepper. (The cheese will add saltiness, so go light on the salt at this stage.)
Transfer salad to a wide, shallow bowl or a large plate and spread out evenly.
Drizzle with more olive oil and a few grinds of black pepper.
notes:
Notes:
This dish greatly depends on the quality of the feta. If you have options at your supermarket, look for true Greek or Bulgarian sheep's-milk feta, which tends to be creamier and tangier than domestic cow's-milk versions. To make this salad more substantial, add arugula.
